answer:
I'm reading your question as **"What is the capacity of cobalt-free batteries?"** If you meant something else, let me know. The most direct data are for the cobalt-free NFA cathode (LiNiₓFeᵧAl_zO₂), with other cobalt-free cathodes covered in the 2022 review.

**NFA cathodes (adma-2020)**
- The NFA compositions deliver about **200 mAh/g** (p. 1).
- First-cycle discharge capacities at C/20 between 3 and 4.5 V (p. 8):
  - NFA 811: about **205 mAh/g**
  - NFA-F: about **199 mAh/g**
  - NFA-A: about **192 mAh/g**
- At a fast 1C rate, NFA-A kept about 116 mAh/g, while NFA-F kept about 81 mAh/g (p. 10).
- Capacity retention after 100 cycles at C/3 (pp. 10–11):
  - NFA-A: about 80%
  - NFA 811: about 70%
  - NFA-F: about 50%
  - Cobalt-containing NCA made the same way: about 68%

**NFA in full pouch cells**
- A 1.5-Ah NFA 811//graphite pouch cell was demonstrated (ensm-2020, p. 8). The material capacity is about 200 mAh/g at 0.1C (p. 7).
- The paper's Table 1 estimates 180 mAh/g and 4–6 mAh/cm² for cobalt-free NFA (ensm-2020, p. 10).
- 0.5-Ah NFA/graphite pouch cells kept 72% of their capacity after 200 cycles at C/3 (aenm-2022, p. 8).

**Other cobalt-free cathodes (aenm-2022)**
- The cobalt-free ternary cathodes NMM, NMT and NMA give more than 200 mAh/g when charged to 4.5 V (p. 8).
- In Mn-substituted LiNiO₂, capacity falls as Mn rises: 212 mAh/g with 10% Mn versus 164 mAh/g with 50% Mn (p. 4).
- LiNiO₂ has a theoretical capacity of about 275 mAh/g (p. 3).
- LiMn₂O₄ gives about 140 mAh/g, and LNMO about 130 mAh/g (p. 9).
- LiFePO₄ gives about 170 mAh/g (p. 9).
- Disordered rock-salt (DRX) cathodes reach up to about 400 mAh/g (p. 9).
